title: Branches, Merging, and Conflict Concepts
learningObjectives: Create a branch for a focused task
Understand branches as pointers to history
Resolve conflicts by reviewing both changes

understand.concept: Branches provide separate lines of work so changes can be developed without immediately altering the shared line. Merging combines histories. A conflict occurs when Git cannot automatically reconcile overlapping edits; a developer must inspect the intended result and test it.
understand.whyItMatters: Reliable workflow and collaboration practices help people coordinate changes, manage risks, and maintain a working project.
understand.analogy: A shared team task benefits when each person understands their responsibility and the agreed steps.
understand.analogyLimit: Development tools and version histories have technical behaviors that this teamwork analogy does not capture.

explain.narrative:
Branches provide separate lines of work so changes can be developed without immediately altering the shared line. Merging combines histories. A conflict occurs when Git cannot automatically reconcile overlapping edits; a developer must inspect the intended result and test it.

Use these practices as a practical guide, adapting them to the repository, language, team, and risk level. Make the intended changes visible and verify them rather than relying on assumptions.
